In triangle $ABC$, what is the value of $\theta ^°$ ?
explanation: Choice C is correct. The tangent of an angle in a right triangle is defined as the ratio of the length of the side opposite the angle to the length of the side adjacent to the angle. In triangle $ABC$, the right angle is at vertex $B$. From the perspective of angle $\theta^{\circ}$ at vertex $C$, the opposite side is $AB$, which has length $3$, and the adjacent side is $BC$, which has length $4$. Therefore, $\tan \theta^{\circ} = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{3}{4}$.
